title: Tenant-level region pinning, retention controls, and automated evidence export for Hosted API
creator: Asha Patel
description: Add first-class tenant-level controls to pin Hosted API data residency to cloud regions, expose per-tenant and per-route retention windows, and provide automated evidence bundles and reporting to satisfy audit requests. This ticket covers product requirements, high-level API shapes, owner/operator rollout strategy, and acceptance criteria; engineering tasks will be split into backend region routing, metadata storage, console UI, and an evidence export job.
background: Customers in regulated industries require guarantees about where inference inputs, cache data, and generated outputs are stored and for how long. Current Hosted API defaults store data in the region chosen by the request routing logic with no tenant-configurable pinning or retention UI. Audit requests today are handled manually by support, which is slow and error-prone. We need a repeatable, auditable control plane for residency and retention and an automated evidence export that codifies proof-of-control for compliance teams.
goals: Allow workspace admins to pin all Hosted API traffic and persisted artifacts to one or more cloud regions (primary + failover regions)
Surface per-tenant default retention windows for request logs, KV cache snapshots, and model outputs, with overrides per-route/token as needed
Provide an automated evidence export feature that bundles residency assertions, retention policy settings, and anonymized sample traces for audits
Ensure controls are compatible with Dedicated and Private offerings (no cross-contamination of guarantees)
Minimize changes required from SDKs — server-side routing and console controls should be sufficient for most customers
non_goals: Implement per-request hard pinning in the SDK — this ticket focuses on admin controls and server routing policies
Full data localization of third-party model assets — out of scope for initial rollout
Rewriting serving runtime — routing will use existing smart-routing with new policy metadata
scope: API: Tenant residency policy CRUD endpoints and per-route retention override fields
Console: New Residency & Retention page in Workspace settings with primary/failover region selector, retention sliders, and evidence export trigger
Backend: Store residency & retention metadata in tenant metadata service, enforce routing during request lifecycle, and mark persisted artifacts with region tags
Export: Batch job to assemble an evidence bundle (JSON + signed assertions + sampled traces) and store it in a customer-visible export location (S3 or secure Drive link)
Telemetry: New metrics for pinned requests, retention overrides, evidence exports, and failures
technical_notes: Residency policy object: {tenant_id, primary_region, failover_regions[], enforce_strict: boolean, retention_defaults: {logs_days, cache_days, outputs_days}} — stored as tenant metadata (stringified JSON in DB)

Routing change: Router will consult tenant metadata at request admission and map to capacity pools with matching region labels. If enforce_strict=true and no matching capacity, return 503 with clear error code.

Retention enforcement: Garbage collector will read tenant retention settings and apply TTL to request logs and persisted caches. Existing data prior to policy creation will be grandfathered with a configurable migration window.

Evidence export: Include signed assertion from control plane containing policy snapshot, timeline of changes (audit log), list of physical compute pools used (anonymized IDs), and a set of 50 sampled request traces with trimmed PII. All exports should be HMAC-signed and logged.
Backward compatibility: Default behavior remains unchanged for tenants without residency policy. SDKs should continue to function; optional client warnings could be added later.
Security: Export artifacts must be access-controlled and encrypted at rest; require workspace admin role to download. Evidence exports should log download events to audit logs.
console_ui: Wireframes: Workspace Settings > Compliance tab > Residency & Retention. Controls: primary region dropdown, add failover region, strict enforcement toggle, retention sliders for logs/cache/outputs (0-365 days), 'Generate evidence export' button with date range selector and export history list.
api_spec: POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/residency  — create/update residency policy (body: primary_region:string, failover_regions:[]string, enforce_strict:boolean, retention_defaults: {logs_days:int, cache_days:int, outputs_days:int})
POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/evidence-exports — request evidence bundle (body: start_date, end_date, include_sampled_traces:boolean)
data_flow: Client request -> API gateway -> Auth -> Admission: read tenant residency metadata cache -> Router selects region-tagged capacity pool -> Serve request in selected region -> persisted artifacts (logs, cache snapshots, outputs) written with region tag and retention TTL -> GC enforces TTL -> Evidence export job aggregates metadata + sampled traces + signed policy snapshot.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (beta): Admin-only console CRUD and non-strict routing (enforce_strict=false). Limited to a pilot list of 10 customers. Collect telemetry and migration feedback.
Phase 2: Add strict enforcement option, expose evidence export in beta, provide migration tooling for existing persisted data. Expand to 50 customers.
Phase 3 (GA): Publicly available residency + retention controls, documented SLAs, and hardened evidence export with RBAC and retention of export artifacts for 30 days.
Migration window: default grandfathering period of 90 days for existing data; admin can invoke accelerated migration via support or dedicated job
acceptance_criteria: Workspace admins can create/update residency policies via console and API
Router respects residency policy for non-strict mode and attributes region tags to persisted artifacts
Garbage collector honors retention_windows set in tenant policy and removes data according to TTL
Evidence export bundle contains policy snapshot, audit log of policy changes, signed assertion, and sampled traces with PII redacted
Export artifacts are encrypted, accessible only to workspace admins, and download events are recorded in audit logs
Unit and integration tests cover routing fallback behavior when requested region capacity is unavailable
Documentation and quickstart for pilot customers are published
risks: Risk: Strict enforcement could cause availability outages if capacity matching tenant region is exhausted. Mitigation: default to non-strict for GA and provide clear error codes and fallbacks.
Risk: Evidence exports may inadvertently include sensitive customer data. Mitigation: sample traces with automated PII redaction and require manual verification for high-risk customers.
Risk: Cross-region dependencies for third-party models or caches not owned by Redwood. Mitigation: document limitations and offer Private/Dedicated guidance.
Risk: Large exports could be expensive and slow. Mitigation: rate-limit exports and provide incremental export slices.
Risk: Confusion between residency (where compute/storage runs) and data sovereignty legal requirements. Mitigation: include legal-approved language in UI and export bundles.
